transcript.text: The supply cart stops by Larkhaven's ranch fence. The whole valley looks faded, like an old picture left in the sun. You too.
There you are! I'm Maren. I keep the ranch. Every tamer signs our register. Write yourself in, love.
As the ink dries, colour runs into you: your hands, your clothes, your hair. You're the only bright thing on the road.
Rowan. Good name. And look at you, bright as a new penny!
Larkhaven farmfolk, it says here. A farm family! Then you know how to look after things that can't tell you what's wrong.
Folk say it comes back, a little, every time someone earns a creature's trust. Come to the barn. Someone's been waiting for you.
Three young ones, born this spring. Go and say hello, love. They'll be choosing you as much as you choose them.
You kneel in the straw. Cindercub looks at you for a long moment, then steps forward and presses its head into your hand.
Colour floods out from it: gold straw, red beams, a blue sky in the high window.
...There. It chose you right back. And the world remembered a little.
Your grandmother always said the land grew tired. People took and took from it, and one hard winter it simply let its colour go. "Look after the land," she'd say, "and one day it'll remember."
Every family in this valley tells it a little differently. I once heard four tellings at one harvest supper. They can't all be right. Maybe they can't all be wrong, either.
Nobody owns a creature, love; they choose. The other two will find their tamers. Wren's due by later, and that one never could wait.
Off you go, then. Show Cindercub the valley.
Outside, the colour has spilled out through the barn door: across the path, up the walls, into the grass.
Cindercub sniffs the bright grass, sneezes, and looks up at you as if to say: where next?
The ranch gate bangs open.
Am I late? Maren, you said the new tamer was coming tomorrow!
I said today, Wren. This is Wren. Same age as you, same first day, and twice the noise.
Hey! So you picked Cindercub? Then I'm taking Ripplet. Don't look at me like that, it's called strategy. Let's battle!
Okay. Okay! Not bad. Ripplet and I were just warming up.
You two will push each other a long way. Now go on, Thornwood won't explore itself. Bring your team back here to rest whenever they need it.
That battle took it out of them — look, they're hurt. I patched them up this time, but the inn in Larkhaven heals your team whenever they need it.
And Rowan? Watch how the wild ones move. Tire one out, toss a lure, and keep it calm. If it trusts you, it will come home with you.
Three can travel with you at a time. The rest live here at the ranch with me, and I look after them. A creature that has bonded with you always finds its way back to you.
One more thing. Here: my old Wilddex. Every creature you meet gets a sketch in it, and every one that bonds with you gets its whole page. Nobody has ever filled one.
Over a hundred kinds live between here and the far coast, and some only come out in the rain, at night, or for tamers they trust. Fill it as far as you can, and bring it back to show me.
A new friend! The ranch has room for them — I look after every creature here, and there's always something useful for a willing one to do. Come by and I'll show you.
Duskweaver joins your team.
